title: Laser-Ablated Au Electrodes with Preferred Orientation and Flat Interface on Oxides
authors: Ambrose Seo, Richard Lai, Sujan Shrestha, Tina Tong, Joseph W. Brill, Menglin Zhu, Chris Chae, Jinwoo Hwang
abstract: Gold (Au) thin-film electrodes deposited on oxides by pulsed laser deposition (PLD) exhibit distinctive structural properties compared with thermally evaporated Au films. While thermally evaporated Au forms polycrystalline films with randomly oriented grains, PLD-grown Au films show a strong preferred [111] orientation perpendicular to the substrate surface, likely due to the energetic nature of the laser-ablated Au plume. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy reveals atomically flat interfaces between the PLD-grown Au electrodes and epitaxial oxide thin films, separated by nanometer-scale gaps comparable to interlayer spacings in van der Waals materials. The highly ordered microstructure and flat interfacial morphology result in enhanced adhesion of the Au films to oxide surfaces. These results demonstrate that PLD can produce both high-quality Au electrodes and oxide thin films within a single deposition platform, offering improved interfacial control and potential benefits for a wide range of oxide electronic and functional devices.
summary: This experimental work compares Au electrodes deposited by Pulsed Laser Deposition (PLD) against those from thermal evaporation on oxide substrates. The authors demonstrate that PLD creates Au films with a highly preferred [111] orientation and atomically flat interfaces. These structural improvements lead to significantly enhanced adhesion, making PLD a superior technique for fabricating high-quality oxide electronic devices.
main_problem: The study aims to improve the interfacial characteristics and adhesion of Gold (Au) electrodes deposited on oxide surfaces for use in electronic devices.
main_result: Pulsed Laser Deposition (PLD) yields Au films with a strong preferred [111] orientation and atomically flat interfaces, resulting in significantly enhanced adhesion compared to thermally evaporated films.
method: The research compares Au films deposited via PLD versus thermal evaporation, using techniques like XRD, HR-TEM, and adhesive tape testing.
model_or_system: The physical system involves Au thin-film electrodes deposited on various oxide substrates (e.g., $	ext{SrTiO}_3$, amorphous silica). The comparison highlights the structural differences induced by the deposition method.
key_observables: Crystallographic orientation (preferred [111] vs. random polycrystalline), interfacial gap size (flat vs. uneven), and macroscopic adhesion strength (tape test).
important_parameters: PLD parameters include $\lambda = 248 	ext{ nm}$ and energy density $= 3 	ext{ J/cm}^2$. The film thickness is around $50 	ext{ nm}$.
main_assumptions: The enhanced adhesion is attributed to the highly energetic nature of the PLD plume, leading to structural texturing and interfacial ordering.
figures_summary: XRD patterns show PLD films exhibit only (111) peaks, while thermal films show multiple peaks. STEM images compare the flat, narrow gap of PLD interfaces to the uneven gaps of thermal interfaces. The tape test compares strong adhesion for PLD films versus weak adhesion for thermal films.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares PLD and thermal deposition methods by analyzing crystal structure (XRD), interface morphology (STEM), and mechanical robustness (tape test) to establish the superior quality of PLD-grown films.
why_interesting: While not directly quantum, the focus on highly controlled, atomically flat interfaces and crystalline texture is crucial for developing quantum devices, as interface quality dictates device performance in quantum electronics.
